title: Make the gateway drop a resent batch

blocks.text: A sensor gateway stores temperature batches and keeps a `HashSet<Batch>` of what it has stored, so that a batch a sensor sends twice (it resends whenever an acknowledgement is lost) is stored once. In production the set never recognises a resent batch, and the gateway's storage has doubled. A second report says that some stored batches later show samples from a different read.
`Batch` is a record with a `String device` and an `int[] samples` component. Finish the four `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Batch.java`:

items: `equals` and `hashCode`: a resent batch is the same device with the same samples in the same order;
`keep(...)`: what the batch stores, given the array the sensor driver passes in (the driver reads every batch into one buffer and reuses it);
`samples()`: what a reader of a stored batch gets back.

blocks.text: When you're done, the gateway's set drops every resent batch, and no code outside `Batch` can change a batch once it is built. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: two batches from the same device with the same samples in the same order are equal; another device, order or length is not
a HashSet that holds a batch refuses a resent copy of it and reports that it contains it
two equal batches built from different arrays have the same hash code
changing the array a batch was built from afterwards doesn't change the batch
changing the array returned by samples() doesn't change the batch or lose it in a set

origin.section: A Record's equals Compares Each Component with Its Own equals, So an Array Compares by Identity

concepts: An array component is mutable, so a record that must not change copies it on the way in and on the way out.
A record's generated equals and hashCode use each component's own equals and hashCode, so an array component compares by identity and two records holding equal arrays are not equal.
